title: Resolution for First-Order Logic
subtopics: More general substitution (partial order on substitutions)

definitions.definition: A substitution σ is a unifier for terms t₁ and t₂ if σ̂(t₁) = σ̂(t₂).
Two terms are unifiable if they have at least one unifier.
A unifier σ₁ is more general than σ₂ if σ₂ = σ₁ ∘ τ for some substitution τ. The MGU is the most general among all unifiers.
The substitution σ₂ ∘ σ₁ defined by (σ₂ ∘ σ₁)(x) = σ̂₂(σ₁(x)).
From clauses C₁ and C₂ (with renamed variables), if L ∈ C₁ and ¬L' ∈ C₂ are unifiable with MGU σ, derive the resolvent σ((C₁ \ {L}) ∪ (C₂ \ {¬L'})).

formulas: FOL Res(C₁, C₂) = σ((C₁ \ {L}) ∪ (C₂ \ {¬L'})) where σ = MGU(L, L')
examples: Unifying f(x, h(y)) and f(h(z), z') with MGU {x ↦ h(z), z' ↦ h(y)}
Showing t₁ = x and t₂ = h(x) are not unifiable (occur check)
exercises: Verify that σ₂ = σ₁ ∘ σ for given substitutions.
Apply FOL resolution to a CSNF formula to check satisfiability.
learning_objectives: Understand and apply Robinson's unification algorithm.
Apply FOL resolution using the MGU to derive resolvents.
